messages: marcus: Heads-up: Docusaurus build on main is failing linkcheck after we flipped the CDN and migrated a few pages from MkDocs -> Docusaurus. Errors: mixed 301/302s and anchors not found on nested docs. dev-bot: [linkcheck] ⚠ 15 redirects detected. Example: /sdk/js#install -> /sdk/js/index.html#install (301) -> https://cdn.redwood.ai/assets/install.png (302). Full log: https://ci.redwood.ai/teams/docs/jobs/9988 anya: Is this the same as the earlier mkdocs CDN relpath bug or different? marcus: Similar surface but different cause: Docusaurus outputs `useHash: true` on some routes and our banner plugin rewrites asset URLs to protocol-relative ones, which then trigger the CDN redirect logic. Browsers sometimes follow the redirects and drop the fragment, so anchors break. li: Can you paste the generated anchor and link? marcus: Generated html: `Install` but the asset link on the page head is ``. The protocol-relative URL causes some tooling to canonicalize to https://cdn... which returns 301 to /assets/... and the fragment gets lost in the roundtrip. harper: Oof. Two quick options: 1) make asset URLs absolute with scheme (https://cdn...) so canonicalization is stable, or 2) avoid protocol-relative URLs and keep assets on the same origin for links that include fragments. anya: For immediate unblock I pushed a tiny change in the build plugin to prefer absolute https CDN URLs for preload/link tags. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/755 dev-bot: [ci] Job 9990 started for PR 755 li: Any chance linkcheck is a false positive because it flags any redirect rather than follow-and-check anchors? harper: Linkcheck flags redirects by design (we treat redirects as a warning/failure). But the anchor loss is real: if a redirect response lacks fragment preservation most clients will drop it. We need the CDN to preserve fragments or avoid redirecting requests that include hashes. marcus: I added a short nginx rule to avoid CDN-edge redirects for requests that contain a hash-like query (we can't see fragment server-side, but we can normalize common paths). As a safer step, the build now emits in-page anchors with full paths that match the final canonical URL (e.g., https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/js/#install). That ensures the anchor survives the redirect. anya: Can you paste the sed I used to rewrite link refs in the static output? marcus: Sure, quick hack in CI: ``` find build -name '*.html' -exec sed -i "s/href=\"\/sdk\/js\/#/href=\"https:\/\/docs.redwood.ai\/sdk\/js#/g" {} + ``` li: Fine as a bandaid for the deploy but we should not ship sed forever. Open a ticket for a theme-level fix. harper: I'll add DOCS-412 to track making Docusaurus canonicalize absolute document links and to update the banner/plugin to emit https CDN URLs for preloads only (not nav links). dev-bot: [ci] Job 9990: linkcheck failures reduced from 15 -> 2 after patch. Job 9992: staging passed. anya: I manually verified fragments on mobile and desktop. Anchors resolve now. marcus: Merging the bandaid to main so the release can go out. Follow-ups: DOCS-412 (theme canonical links), DOCS-413 (CDN redirect policy), DOCS-414 (update linkcheck to follow single-redirects for anchors). Closing out this thread, moving details to ticket. :white_check_mark:
